Financial_Insti.name: Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO)
Financial_Insti.description: Government agency that gives financial help to people with health problems through its Medical Assistance Program, together with government and private hospitals, health facilities and medicine retailers.

branches.location: Maharlika Center, J.P Cabagui Avenue, Davao City

eligibility: Individuals with health-related problems seeking financial help
programs.program_description: Financial help for patients, given in partnership with government and private hospitals, health facilities, medicine retailers and other partners. Cancer treatment (chemotherapy drugs, immunotherapy and radiation therapy) is one of the types of help. If approved, the patient gets a Guarantee Letter (GL) for the hospital, health facility, medicine retailer or diagnostic center.

benefits.benefit_name: Cancer treatment: chemotherapeutic drugs and immunotherapy
Laboratory, diagnostic and imaging procedures (such as CT-Scan, MRI, PET Scan and biopsy)

requirements.requirement_description: Valid proof of identity of the patient (government-issued ID or other accepted ID)
Valid ID of the patient's next of kin, if applicable

For cancer treatment: updated clinical or medical abstract (issued within the past 3 months), medical prescription, and treatment protocol (chemotherapy) or treatment plan (radiation therapy), each with the full name, signature and license number of the attending physician
For cancer treatment: one quotation from the hospital willing to accept the GL, or official quotations from three different suppliers if the medicine is not available in the hospital

procedure.instruction: Apply online through the Online MAP Application (steps 2 to 6), or go to the PCSO Davao City Branch, or to the PCSO or Malasakit Center desk of your hospital. In some areas, MAP can be accessed only through hospitals with a Malasakit Center.
Go to www.pcso.gov.ph, select "E-Services", then "Online MAP Application", and create an account.
Log in with your name, date of birth and email, and enter the one-time code sent to your email.
Click "Apply Now", choose the partner health facility, its city and the type of request, then get a queuing number.
Upload all required documents as PDF files (not more than 2MB each) and submit the application.
Wait for the result in your email or in your online account.

Financial_Insti.name: Department of Health (DOH)
Financial_Insti.description: National government department for health. Its MAIFIP program helps pay the medical bills of patients who cannot afford them, and its Cancer Assistance Fund (CAF) and CSPMAP help cancer patients with treatment and free medicines.

branches.location: PRRD Bldg Bajada, Davao City (infront SPMC Hospital)
Malasakit Center, Bajada, Davao City (beside SPMC Hospital)

programs.program_name: Medical Assistance for Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients (MAIFIP)
eligibility: Indigent and financially incapacitated patients who cannot afford their medical expenses
Including PhilHealth members whose remaining bill is still too big
programs.program_description: Covers the remaining out-of-pocket hospital bill after PhilHealth and other discounts. DOH Davao says there is no fixed maximum amount, and payment is targeted within 12 working days when documents are complete (2026). Cancer patients at SPMC have used it for laboratories, CT scans, procedures and medicines.

benefits.benefit_name: Remaining medical bill after PhilHealth and other discounts

requirements.requirement_description: Unified Intake Sheet (evaluated by a social worker)
Final bill or statement of account (in-patient), or price quotation and doctor's prescription (out-patient)
Medical certificate or patient's clinical summary / medical abstract
Copy of IDs (patient and/or patient's representative)

procedure.instruction: Go to the Malasakit Center or the Medical Social Work Unit (MSW) of your hospital, or apply online through eMAIFIP in the eGovPH app. eMAIFIP started in DOH hospitals and is being extended to LGU hospitals.
Ask the hospital's social worker to assess you for MAIFIP. The social worker evaluates your Unified Intake Sheet.
Submit the documents the social worker asks for. Payment is faster when the documents are complete.

eligibility: Persons with cancer, cancer survivors and high-risk individuals
For the eight priority cancer types
programs.program_description: DOH fund under RA 11215 (National Integrated Cancer Control Act). It pays for cancer prevention, screening, early detection and diagnosis, treatment and care-related components for 8 priority cancer types. It adds to PhilHealth and other help for costs they do not cover, and for cancer cases it is used before MAIP. In Davao City, Southern Philippines Medical Center is a CAF access site (one of 36 nationwide, July 2026).
cancerTypes: Liver cancer, including colorectal and other digestive tract cancers
Head and neck cancers, including thyroid
Prostate, renal and urinary bladder cancer

requirements.requirement_description: Medical abstract, doctor's prescription, or treatment plan

procedure.instruction: Go to a CAF access site. In Davao City: Southern Philippines Medical Center.
Present your medical abstract, doctor's prescription, or treatment plan to the social worker assigned to the hospital for assessment and approval.
Your documents are evaluated before approval and availment of services.

programs.program_name: Cancer and Supportive-Palliative Medicines Access Program (CSPMAP)
programs.program_description: DOH program that gives free medicines not yet covered by PhilHealth, to lower or remove out-of-pocket costs. It is part of the National Integrated Cancer Control Program. Its DOH hospital access sites are also CAF access sites. In 2024, 35 access sites offered 61 medicines for the most common cancers.

benefits.benefit_name: Free medicines not yet covered by PhilHealth
